newsitem.title: CHILE: SBC may quit Chile telecom - report.
newsitem.headline: SBC may quit Chile telecom - report.

text.p: Southwestern Bell may withdraw its stake in Chilean telecom and cable operator VTR SA if talks about a merger between VTR and Telecomunicaciones de Chile, or CTC, move ahead, a Santiago newspaper report said.

The financial daily El Diario quoted sources close to the VTR-CTC talks as saying that CTC's main shareholder Telefonica de Espana was demanding SBC sell its shares in VTR as a condition for a planned merger with CTC.
SBC bought into VTR in 1995 by purchasing 40 percent of its shares from the Luksic family for $316.6 million, with the controlling stake still held by the Luksics.

El Diario said a CTC-VTR deal would be worth about $900 million and that San Antonio-based SBC would be paid according to the current value of its shares in VTR, or about $400 million, with no additional money.
SBC is one of two major U.S. telecommunications companies in Chile, the other being Atlanta-based BellSouth.
